name: Oudhyana
why_it_matters: Taj Mahal Lucknow's Awadhi specialty room — the city's only fine-dining setup running the slow-cooked Awadhi cuisine in full pomp, with live ghazal-style music nightly. Subtle spicing built around hours of dum and yakhni reduction, the way Lucknow's tehzeeb school of cooks practised it.
insider_tip: Lunch service is much quieter; book 12:30-3pm for a calmer kitchen pace. The galouti and ulte-tawa paratha pairing is the dish to test the kitchen on.
signature_address: Taj Mahal Lucknow, Vipin Khand, Gomti Nagar, Lucknow 226010

name: Falaknuma
why_it_matters: The rooftop a-la-carte of Hotel Clarks Avadh — sightlines onto the Gomti and Chhatar Manzil Palace. Live ghazal accompaniment most nights; the kitchen leans Awadhi but the view is the bigger sell. Not a revolving restaurant despite local description.
insider_tip: Sunset table is non-negotiable — call ahead for a window seat at 6pm. Afternoon service is slower (12:30-3:30pm) and view-only; dinner has the ghazal.
signature_address: Hotel Clarks Avadh, 8 Mahatma Gandhi Marg, Hazratganj, Lucknow 226001
